## E01 · Project Foundation

**Goal:** A working, deployable Next.js + Supabase skeleton with tooling and CI so every later epic can ship small PRs safely.  
**Milestone:** M1 · Walking skeleton  
**Source:** [epics/E01-foundation.md](epics/E01-foundation.md)

### E01-T01 · Bootstrap Next.js app — S

**Why:** Every other task needs a consistent codebase with the same structure, lint rules and scripts, so reviews focus on behavior rather than style.

**Scope**
- Create the app with `create-next-app`: App Router, TypeScript (`strict: true`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true`), `src/` directory, Tailwind CSS.
- ESLint (Next.js + TypeScript rules, `import/order`, no unused vars) and Prettier (with the Tailwind class-sorting plugin).
- Path alias `@/*` → `src/*`.
- Create the empty folder structure from [architecture.md](architecture.md#code-structure) (`app/[locale]`, `components/ui`, `components/common`, `features/*`, `lib/*`, `types/`), each with a `.gitkeep` or short README.
- npm scripts: `dev`, `build`, `start`, `lint`, `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`), `format`, `format:check`.
- `.nvmrc` with the Node LTS version; `engines` field in `package.json`.
- Root README: prerequisites, install, run, and a link to `docs/`.

**Out of scope:** Auth, database, i18n and theming (separate tasks).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A fresh clone runs with `npm ci && npm run dev` and shows a placeholder page at `http://localhost:3000`.
- [ ] `npm run build`, `lint`, `typecheck` and `format:check` all pass with zero warnings.
- [ ] Introducing an unused variable or wrong import order makes `lint` fail.
- [ ] Folder structure matches the architecture doc.
- [ ] README setup steps work for a new developer without extra help.

**Depends on:** —

### E01-T02 · Supabase local setup & migrations workflow — S

**Why:** The schema must be versioned and reproducible so every developer, CI run and environment has the same database.

**Scope**
- `supabase init`; commit `supabase/config.toml`.
- First migration enables extensions `pg_trgm` and `unaccent` and creates an `immutable` wrapper function `f_unaccent(text)` (needed for generated columns and indexes).
- npm scripts: `db:start`, `db:stop`, `db:reset` (applies migrations + `seed.sql`), `db:new <name>`, `db:types` (writes `src/types/database.ts`).
- Empty `supabase/seed.sql` (filled in later epics).
- `.env.example` with every variable from the architecture doc and a one-line comment each.

**Out of scope:** Any application tables (they come with their feature epics).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `npm run db:start` starts local Supabase (Docker) and prints the local URL and keys.
- [ ] `npm run db:reset` drops and rebuilds the database from migrations without errors.
- [ ] `npm run db:types` creates `src/types/database.ts`, and running it twice produces no diff.
- [ ] `select f_unaccent('Ąžuolas')` returns `Azuolas`.
- [ ] `.env.example` contains every variable the app reads; no real secrets are committed.

**Depends on:** E01-T01

### E01-T03 · Supabase client helpers — S

**Why:** One place to create Supabase clients keeps token handling, typing and the service-role key safe and consistent.

**Scope**
- `lib/supabase/server.ts`: `createServerClient()` for Server Components, Server Actions and Route Handlers.
- `lib/supabase/client.ts`: `createBrowserClient()` for client components (singleton per tab).
- Both typed with `Database` from generated types and accept an `accessToken` callback (wired to Clerk in E04-T02; until then a stub).
- `lib/supabase/admin.ts`: service-role client, guarded with `import 'server-only'`, used only by webhooks/admin jobs.

**Out of scope:** Clerk integration itself (E04-T02).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A Server Component can query a test table through `createServerClient()` with full type inference (wrong column names fail `typecheck`).
- [ ] Importing `lib/supabase/admin.ts` from a client component fails the build.
- [ ] The service-role key does not appear in the client bundle (checked by grepping `.next/static`).
- [ ] Helpers have JSDoc explaining when to use each one.

**Depends on:** E01-T02 (token wiring finalized in E04-T02)

### E01-T04 · Testing setup — M

**Why:** RLS rules, metrics and logging flows are easy to break; automated tests at three levels (unit, database, end-to-end) catch this before release.

**Scope**
- **Unit/component:** Vitest + React Testing Library + `jsdom`; `npm test`, `npm run test:watch`, coverage report.
- **Database/RLS:** a test helper that signs JWTs for fake user ids (`sub`) with the local Supabase JWT secret, so tests can act as user A or B against local Supabase; `npm run test:db`.
- **E2E:** Playwright (Chromium + WebKit mobile viewport), `npm run e2e`; Clerk testing tokens plus a helper `signInAs(user)` that skips the Google UI.
- Test data factories (`createUser`, later `createSession`, …) in `tests/factories`.
- One passing example test of each kind.

**Out of scope:** Real feature tests (written with each feature).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `npm test`, `npm run test:db` and `npm run e2e` each run and pass on a clean checkout with local Supabase running.
- [ ] The example RLS test proves user B cannot read user A's row in a sample table.
- [ ] The example e2e test signs in a test user without the Google consent screen.
- [ ] Each test run starts from a known database state (reset or transaction rollback); tests don't depend on run order.
- [ ] Testing approach is documented in `docs/` or `tests/README.md`.

**Depends on:** E01-T02

### E01-T05 · CI pipeline — S

**Why:** Every PR must prove it builds, passes tests and keeps the schema valid before merge.

**Scope**
- GitHub Actions workflow on `pull_request` and `push` to `main`.
- Jobs: install (npm cache) → lint + typecheck + `format:check` → unit tests → start Supabase CLI, apply migrations on an empty DB, run `test:db` → `build` → Playwright e2e (upload report and traces on failure).
- Check that generated DB types are up to date (`db:types` then `git diff --exit-code`).
- Branch protection on `main`: required checks + 1 review.

**Out of scope:** Deployment (E01-T06).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A PR with a lint error, type error, failing test or broken migration is blocked from merging.
- [ ] A PR that changes a migration without regenerating types fails with a clear message.
- [ ] Playwright HTML report is downloadable from failed runs.
- [ ] Typical pipeline finishes in under ~8 minutes.

**Depends on:** E01-T04

### E01-T06 · Environments & deployment — S

**Why:** Product and testers need a link to every change, and production releases must be repeatable and safe.

**Scope**
- Vercel project linked to the repo: preview deployment per PR, production on `main`.
- Supabase projects: **staging** (used by previews) and **production**.
- GitHub Action on merge to `main`: `supabase db push` to production before the Vercel production build is promoted; staging gets migrations on every PR merge to `main` too.
- Secrets set in Vercel/GitHub per environment.
- Short runbook in `docs/` (how to deploy, roll back, run a migration manually).

**Out of scope:** Custom domain and production Clerk instance (E10-T07).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Every PR shows a preview URL that works against staging.
- [ ] Merging to `main` applies new migrations to production and deploys the app without manual steps.
- [ ] A failed migration stops the production deploy.
- [ ] No secret values exist in the repository or build logs.
- [ ] The runbook explains how to roll back to the previous deployment.

**Depends on:** E01-T05

### E01-T07 · Error tracking & shared Result type — S

**Why:** We need to know when something breaks in production, and every Server Action should return errors in the same shape so the UI can show translated messages.

**Scope**
- Error tracking (e.g. Sentry) for client, server and edge runtimes; release tagged with commit SHA; source maps uploaded; PII scrubbing (no emails in events).
- `lib/result.ts`: `type Result<T> = { ok: true; data: T } | { ok: false; error: ErrorCode; fields?: Record<string, ErrorCode> }` and helpers `ok()`, `fail()`.
- `ErrorCode` enum (`UNAUTHORIZED`, `FORBIDDEN`, `NOT_FOUND`, `VALIDATION`, `CONFLICT`, `LOCKED`, `UNKNOWN`) mapped to i18n keys `errors.*`.
- `withAction()` wrapper: validates input with zod, catches errors, reports unexpected ones, returns `Result`.

**Out of scope:** Alerting rules (E10-T07).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A test error thrown in a Server Component and in a client component both appear in error tracking with the release tag and readable stack trace.
- [ ] Events contain no email addresses or auth tokens.
- [ ] An example Server Action using `withAction()` returns `{ ok: false, error: 'VALIDATION', fields }` for invalid input (unit tested).
- [ ] Every `ErrorCode` has an `errors.*` key (checked once i18n exists).

**Depends on:** E01-T01

## E02 · Design System & Theming

**Goal:** A calm, earth-tone, minimal UI kit with light and dark modes, used consistently across the app.  
**Milestone:** M1 · Walking skeleton  
**Source:** [epics/E02-design-system.md](epics/E02-design-system.md)

### E02-T01 · Design tokens & Tailwind theme — M

**Why:** Colors, spacing and type must be defined once so the whole app stays calm and consistent and both themes work automatically.

**Scope**
- CSS variables in `app/globals.css` for every semantic token in the design doc, under `:root` (light) and `.dark` (dark).
- Tailwind config maps tokens to utilities (`bg-background`, `text-muted-foreground`, `bg-primary`, `chart-1…5`, …).
- Radius (`8px` controls, `12px` cards), spacing (4 px grid), font sizes from the type scale.
- Inter loaded via `next/font` with the `latin-ext` subset (Lithuanian letters).
- `tabular-nums` utility for numbers.
- Script `npm run check:contrast` that computes WCAG contrast for the key token pairs in both themes.
- Lint rule or CI grep that fails on raw hex/rgb colors outside the token file.

**Out of scope:** Theme switching UI (E02-T02); individual components (E02-T03).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Every semantic token from the design doc has a light and a dark value.
- [ ] `check:contrast` passes: body text ≥ 4.5:1, large text and UI borders/icons ≥ 3:1, in both themes.
- [ ] Lithuanian text "ąčęėįšųūž ĄČĘĖĮŠŲŪŽ" renders in Inter with no fallback font.
- [ ] Adding `color: #ff0000` in a component makes CI fail.
- [ ] Palette visually reviewed and signed off by the product owner (screenshot of tokens page in both themes).

**Depends on:** E01-T01

### E02-T02 · Light / dark mode — S

**Why:** Users train in bright gyms and dark rooms; they need to choose a theme or follow the OS setting.

**Scope**
- `next-themes` provider with `attribute="class"`, options `light`, `dark`, `system` (default `system`).
- `ThemeToggle` component (3 options with icons and labels) used in the avatar menu and on the landing page.
- No flash of the wrong theme on first load (script injected before paint).
- `<meta name="theme-color">` updated per theme (browser UI color on mobile).
- Hook to save the choice to `profiles.theme` once logged in (wired in E04-T04).

**Out of scope:** Per-user server-side persistence (E04-T04).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Switching theme updates the whole UI immediately without reload.
- [ ] The choice survives a page reload and a browser restart (local storage).
- [ ] With `system`, changing the OS theme updates the app live.
- [ ] Hard reload in dark mode shows no white flash (verified on throttled connection).
- [ ] Toggle is keyboard accessible and announces the current theme to screen readers.

**Depends on:** E02-T01

### E02-T03 · Base UI components — M

**Why:** A shared, accessible component set keeps the UI minimal and avoids each feature styling its own buttons and dialogs.

**Scope**
- Add via shadcn/ui and restyle with tokens: Button (`primary`, `secondary`, `ghost`, `destructive`; `sm`/`md`/`lg`; loading state), Input, Textarea, Label, FormField (label + help + error), Card, Dialog, Sheet (bottom sheet on mobile), Popover, Tabs, SegmentedControl, Toast, Avatar + AvatarStack, Chip/Badge (optionally removable), Skeleton, DropdownMenu, EmptyState.
- Icons from `lucide-react` at 20 px, 1.5 px stroke.
- Dev-only page `/dev/ui` showing every component and variant, with a theme toggle.
- Component tests for interactive pieces (Dialog focus trap, removable Chip).

**Out of scope:** Combobox and NumberStepper (own tasks).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] All listed components exist, use only semantic tokens, and look correct in both themes on `/dev/ui`.
- [ ] Every interactive component is usable with keyboard only and has a visible focus ring (`--ring`).
- [ ] Dialog/Sheet trap focus, close on `Esc`, and return focus to the trigger.
- [ ] Touch targets are at least 44 × 44 px on mobile sizes.
- [ ] `/dev/ui` is not reachable in production builds.

**Depends on:** E02-T01

### E02-T04 · Searchable Combobox component — M

**Why:** The core interaction for choosing exercises, machines, tags and buddies is a searchable dropdown with a "create new" option. Building it once makes all those pickers behave the same.

**Scope**
- Generic `Combobox<T>` built from Popover + `cmdk` Command.
- Props: `onSearch(query) => Promise<T[]>`, `renderItem`, `getKey`, `getLabel`, `value`/`onChange`, `multiple`, `allowCreate`, `onCreate(query)`, `placeholder`, `emptyText`, `initialItems` (shown before typing).
- 200 ms debounce, request cancellation (only the latest result is shown), loading spinner, empty state.
- Sticky footer item **"Create '{query}'"** shown when `allowCreate` and no result's normalized label equals the normalized query (lowercase, trimmed, accents removed).
- Match highlighting that is accent-insensitive.
- Multi-select shows selected items as removable chips in the trigger.
- On mobile, opens as a full-height sheet with the input focused.

**Out of scope:** The data sources (exercise search etc. are separate tasks).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Typing filters results after 200 ms; fast typing does not show stale results (unit test with delayed mock).
- [ ] `↑`/`↓` move the highlight, `Enter` selects, `Esc` closes; the create item is reachable by keyboard.
- [ ] Query "spaudimas" highlights "Špaudimas" and "spaudimas"; "Create" is hidden when an exact normalized match exists, shown otherwise.
- [ ] Choosing "Create '{query}'" calls `onCreate` with the trimmed query.
- [ ] Screen readers announce the number of results and the active option (ARIA combobox pattern).
- [ ] Works on iOS Safari without the keyboard covering the results list.

**Depends on:** E02-T03

### E02-T05 · NumberStepper component — S

**Why:** Weight and reps are entered with sweaty hands between sets; big − / + buttons and a numeric keyboard make this fast and error-free.

**Scope**
- `NumberStepper` with props `value`, `onChange`, `step`, `min`, `max`, `decimals`, `unit` (e.g. "kg"), `label`.
- Big − / + buttons (≥ 44 px) with long-press auto-repeat (accelerating).
- Text input with `inputmode="decimal"` (weight) or `numeric` (reps); accepts both `,` and `.`; shows the locale separator (`,` in LT, `.` in EN).
- Value clamped to min/max on blur; invalid input reverts to the last valid value.
- Presets: weight (step 2.5, min 0, max 999.75, 2 decimals), reps (step 1, min 1, max 999).

**Out of scope:** lb conversion (post-MVP).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Typing `57,5` or `57.5` both store `57.5`; displays `57,5` in LT and `57.5` in EN.
- [ ] Holding + for 2 s increases the value repeatedly and faster over time; releasing stops it.
- [ ] Values below min or above max are clamped on blur.
- [ ] Mobile shows a numeric keypad.
- [ ] Has an accessible label and announces the new value on change.

**Depends on:** E02-T03

### E02-T06 · App layout & navigation — M

**Why:** Users need a simple, predictable way to move between the four main areas on both phone and desktop.

**Scope**
- Authenticated layout for `(app)` routes.
- Mobile (< 1024 px): fixed bottom navigation with **Home**, **Sessions**, **Progress**, **Buddies** (icon + label, safe-area padding for iPhones).
- Desktop (≥ 1024 px): left sidebar with the same items; content max width 1120 px.
- Header: page title, back button on detail pages, avatar menu (language, theme, settings, sign out).
- Badge slot on nav items (used by E05-T03 and E07-T03).
- Shared page patterns: `PageHeader`, `PageSkeleton`, `EmptyState` usage, `loading.tsx`/`error.tsx` per section.
- Placeholder pages for the four sections.

**Out of scope:** The content of each section.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] The active section is highlighted in both bottom nav and sidebar.
- [ ] Layout works from 360 px to 1440 px wide with no horizontal scroll.
- [ ] Bottom nav is not hidden behind the iPhone home indicator.
- [ ] All nav labels are translated (EN/LT) and the menu works with keyboard.
- [ ] Each section shows a skeleton while loading and a friendly translated error page on failure.

**Depends on:** E02-T03, E03-T01

## E03 · Internationalization (EN / LT)

**Goal:** The whole UI is available in English and Lithuanian, with locale-aware dates, numbers and plurals.  
**Milestone:** M1 · Walking skeleton  
**Source:** [epics/E03-i18n.md](epics/E03-i18n.md)

### E03-T01 · next-intl setup & locale routing — M

**Why:** All features need a translation mechanism from day one; adding it later means rewriting every screen.

**Scope**
- Install `next-intl`; routes under `app/[locale]/…` with locales `en` and `lt`, default `lt`.
- Middleware that combines next-intl locale detection with Clerk's auth middleware (one `middleware.ts`).
- Locale chosen in this order: URL → `NEXT_LOCALE` cookie → saved profile locale → `Accept-Language` → `lt`.
- `messages/en.json` and `messages/lt.json` with namespaces per feature (`common`, `nav`, `auth`, `buddies`, `sessions`, `exercises`, `logging`, `progress`, `settings`, `errors`).
- TypeScript type-safe message keys (`global.d.ts` augmentation).
- `<html lang>` set to the active locale; localized `<title>` and meta description.

**Out of scope:** Language switcher UI (E03-T02); formatting helpers (E03-T03).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Opening `/` with a Lithuanian browser redirects to `/lt`; with an English browser to `/en`; otherwise to `/lt`.
- [ ] Server Components (`getTranslations`) and client components (`useTranslations`) both render translated text.
- [ ] Using a key that doesn't exist fails `typecheck`.
- [ ] `<html lang>` is `lt` or `en` to match the URL.
- [ ] Protected routes still require sign-in under both locales.

**Depends on:** E01-T01

### E03-T02 · Language switcher & persistence — S

**Why:** Users must be able to change language at any time, and their choice should follow them across devices.

**Scope**
- `LanguageSwitcher` (LT / EN, shown with native names "Lietuvių" / "English") in the avatar menu and on the landing page.
- Switching replaces the locale in the current URL, keeping path and query params.
- Saves to the `NEXT_LOCALE` cookie; when signed in, also updates `profiles.locale` via Server Action.
- On sign-in, if `profiles.locale` differs from the URL, redirect to the saved locale.

**Out of scope:** Translating user-created content.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Switching on `/lt/sessions/123?tab=x` leads to `/en/sessions/123?tab=x`.
- [ ] After switching to EN on phone, signing in on desktop opens the app in EN.
- [ ] Switching is keyboard accessible and the current language is indicated.
- [ ] Clerk components (sign-in, user menu) switch language too.

**Depends on:** E03-T01, E04-T04

### E03-T03 · Formatting helpers — S

**Why:** Dates, numbers and plurals look different in Lithuanian and English; wrong formats feel broken to users.

**Scope**
- `useFormat()` / `getFormat()` wrapping next-intl formatters with presets:
  - `weight(57.5)` → "57,5 kg" (LT) / "57.5 kg" (EN)
  - `date(d)`, `dateTime(d)`, `relative(d)` ("prieš 2 dienas" / "2 days ago")
  - `duration(minutes)` → "1 val. 15 min." / "1 h 15 min"
- ICU plural messages for common counts (sets, reps, sessions, exercises, buddies), using Lithuanian forms one / few / many / other.
- Times shown in the user's browser timezone; timezone passed from client to server via cookie for SSR consistency.

**Out of scope:** Unit conversion.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] LT plurals render correctly: "1 serija", "2 serijos", "10 serijų", "21 serija", "1,5" (decimals use "other").
- [ ] EN plurals: "1 set", "2 sets".
- [ ] Weights and dates follow the active locale in both server and client renders (no hydration mismatch warnings).
- [ ] Unit tests cover all presets in both locales.

**Depends on:** E03-T01

### E03-T04 · Missing-key check in CI — S

**Why:** It's easy to add an English string and forget the Lithuanian one; CI should catch it.

**Scope**
- Script `npm run i18n:check` that compares the key trees of `en.json` and `lt.json` and reports keys missing in either file, empty values, and ICU syntax errors.
- Added to the CI lint job.
- Short contributor note in the docs: how to add a new string.

**Out of scope:** Machine translation.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Adding a key only to `en.json` fails CI and the output lists the missing key path and file.
- [ ] An empty string value or broken ICU syntax (e.g. unclosed `{count, plural`) fails the check.
- [ ] The check runs in under 5 seconds.

**Depends on:** E03-T01, E01-T05

### E03-T05 · Translated catalog content — S

**Why:** Seeded tags and common exercises should appear in the user's language, while user-created names stay as they were typed.

**Scope**
- Tags show `label_lt` or `label_en` depending on the active locale.
- Seeded exercises and machines get Lithuanian names and descriptions via `exercise_translations` / `machine_translations` (decision Q2).
- Search (E06-T02) matches the original name and all translations.
- Display rule: show the translation for the active locale if it exists, otherwise the original name.

**Out of scope:** Users translating their own exercises.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] With LT active, the "chest" tag shows as "Krūtinė"; with EN, "Chest".
- [ ] Searching "spaudimas" and "bench press" both find the seeded "Bench press".
- [ ] User-created exercises show their original name in both locales.
- [ ] Every seeded tag, machine and exercise has both EN and LT text (seed test).

**Depends on:** E06-T01

## E04 · Authentication & Profile

**Goal:** Users sign in with Google, get a profile automatically, and every DB request is authorized by RLS using their Clerk identity.  
**Milestone:** M1 · Walking skeleton  
**Source:** [epics/E04-auth.md](epics/E04-auth.md)

### E04-T01 · Clerk with Google sign-in — S

**Why:** Google login is the only sign-in method required; it removes passwords and makes joining a friend's session quick.

**Scope**
- Clerk application (dev instance) with **Google** as the only enabled method; email/password and other providers disabled.
- `<ClerkProvider>` in the root layout with `localization` set from the active locale (`ltLT` / `enUS`) and `appearance` using design tokens.
- Sign-in page `/[locale]/sign-in` with Clerk `<SignIn />`; after sign-in redirect to `/[locale]` Home, or to the originally requested URL.
- Middleware protects every route in `(app)`; public: landing, sign-in, `/api/webhooks/*`.
- Sign out from the avatar menu.

**Out of scope:** Profile table (E04-T03).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Opening `/lt/sessions` while signed out redirects to sign-in, then back to `/lt/sessions` after Google login.
- [ ] Only the "Continue with Google" option is visible.
- [ ] Sign-in works on desktop Chrome, Android Chrome and iOS Safari.
- [ ] Sign-in UI is in Lithuanian under `/lt` and English under `/en`, and matches the light/dark theme.
- [ ] Signing out clears the session and returns to the landing page.

**Depends on:** E01-T01, E03-T01

### E04-T02 · Clerk ↔ Supabase integration — S

**Why:** Supabase must know who the user is on every request, so RLS can enforce privacy in the database rather than in app code only.

**Scope**
- Add Clerk as a **third-party auth provider** in Supabase (local `config.toml`, staging, production) and activate the Supabase integration in Clerk.
- Supabase clients (E01-T03) pass `accessToken: async () => (await auth()).getToken()` on the server and `session.getToken()` in the browser.
- SQL helper `uid()` returning `auth.jwt()->>'sub'` (`stable`), used by all RLS policies.
- Local development: RLS test helper signs equivalent JWTs (E01-T04).

**Out of scope:** Profile sync (E04-T03).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] With a test table protected by `using (owner_id = uid())`, a signed-in user reads only their own rows.
- [ ] A request without a token (anonymous) gets zero rows from protected tables and cannot insert.
- [ ] A forged or expired token is rejected by Supabase.
- [ ] Works the same in local, preview and production environments.

**Depends on:** E04-T01, E01-T03

### E04-T03 · Profiles table & sync — M

**Why:** Other users need to see a name and avatar (buddies, sessions), and the app needs to store preferences such as language and theme.

**Scope**
- Migration for `profiles` (see [data-model.md](data-model.md#profiles)) with RLS: users can read and update their own profile; visibility to buddies and co-participants is added in E05-T01 / E07-T01.
- Users may update only `locale` and `theme`; `display_name`, `email`, `avatar_url` come from Clerk.
- Route `/api/webhooks/clerk` handling `user.created`, `user.updated`, `user.deleted`, verified with the Svix signature, writing via the service-role client.
- Fallback: on the first authenticated request, if no profile exists, create it from Clerk's `currentUser()`.
- Webhook is idempotent (repeated events give the same result).

**Out of scope:** Full GDPR deletion of related data (E10-T05).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A brand-new Google user has a `profiles` row within 5 seconds of first sign-in, even if the webhook is delayed.
- [ ] Changing the Google account name/photo updates `display_name`/`avatar_url` after the next `user.updated` event.
- [ ] A request with a missing or invalid Svix signature returns 401 and changes nothing.
- [ ] Replaying the same webhook event twice doesn't create duplicates or errors.
- [ ] RLS tests: user A cannot read or update user B's profile (before they are buddies).
- [ ] A user cannot change their own `email` or `display_name` through the API.

**Depends on:** E04-T02

### E04-T04 · Settings page — S

**Why:** Users need one place to see their account and set language and theme preferences that follow them across devices.

**Scope**
- `/[locale]/settings` with sections:
  - **Account:** avatar, name, email (read-only, "Managed by Google"), link to Clerk's account management.
  - **Preferences:** language (LT/EN), theme (light/dark/system).
  - **Sign out.**
  - Placeholder for "Export data" and "Delete account" (filled in E10-T05).
- Saving preferences via a Server Action updating `profiles`; changes apply immediately.
- On sign-in on a new device, `profiles.theme` and `profiles.locale` are applied.

**Out of scope:** Data export and deletion (E10-T05).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Changing theme or language applies instantly and shows a short "Saved" confirmation.
- [ ] Preferences set on one device are applied when signing in on another.
- [ ] Email and name are visible but cannot be edited.
- [ ] Page works in both locales and themes and at 360 px width.

**Depends on:** E04-T03, E02-T02

### E04-T05 · Public landing page — S

**Why:** The first screen for new users should explain the app in one glance and make signing in a single tap.

**Scope**
- `/[locale]` for signed-out users: app name/logo, one-line value proposition, 3 short benefit points (train with buddies, last attempt pre-filled, see progress), "Continue with Google" button, language switch and theme toggle.
- Signed-in users visiting `/[locale]` see Home instead.
- Basic SEO: title, description, Open Graph image (earth-tone), per locale.

**Out of scope:** Marketing site, blog, pricing.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Signed-out visitors see the landing page; signed-in users are sent to Home.
- [ ] "Continue with Google" starts Google sign-in directly (one tap).
- [ ] All text is translated; layout works in both themes and at 360 px.
- [ ] Lighthouse mobile scores ≥ 90 for performance and accessibility.

**Depends on:** E04-T01, E02-T03

## E05 · Gym Buddies

**Goal:** Users build a friend list ("gym buddies") through requests that the other person accepts.  
**Milestone:** M2 · Train together  
**Source:** [epics/E05-gym-buddies.md](epics/E05-gym-buddies.md)

### E05-T01 · Buddy schema, RLS & helpers — M

**Why:** Buddy connections decide who can see whose profile and who can be invited to sessions, so the rules must live in the database.

**Scope**
- Migration for `buddy_connections` (see [data-model.md](data-model.md#buddy_connections)) with status enum `pending | accepted | declined`.
- Constraints: no self-requests; one row per pair regardless of direction (unique index on `least/greatest`).
- RLS:
  - SELECT: requester or addressee.
  - INSERT: only as `requester_id = uid()` with status `pending`.
  - UPDATE: only the addressee, only `pending → accepted | declined`, sets `responded_at`.
  - DELETE: either side (cancel request or remove buddy).
- `are_buddies(a, b)` SQL function (`security definer`, `stable`).
- `search_users(query)` RPC: exact email match or display-name prefix (≥ 3 chars), excludes self, max 20 results, returns `id, display_name, avatar_url, relation` (`none | pending_out | pending_in | buddy`). Does not return emails.
- Extend `profiles` SELECT policy: visible to buddies and to users with a pending request either way.
- A declined request can be sent again after 30 days (prevents spam).

**Out of scope:** UI.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] RLS tests: user C cannot see or change a connection between A and B.
- [ ] Only the addressee can accept or decline; the requester trying to accept gets an error.
- [ ] Sending a request to yourself, or a second request for the same pair, is rejected.
- [ ] `search_users` never returns an email field, and never returns the caller.
- [ ] `are_buddies(A, B)` is true only for `accepted` connections, in both directions.
- [ ] After a decline, a new request from the same requester is rejected for 30 days.

**Depends on:** E04-T03

### E05-T02 · Find users & send request — M

**Why:** Users need to find their friends in the app and connect with them quickly.

**Scope**
- "Add buddy" button on the Buddies page opens a sheet with a search field (uses `search_users`).
- Result rows: avatar, name, and an action depending on relation: **Send request**, **Requested** (disabled, with cancel), **Accept** (if they already requested you), **Buddies** (disabled).
- If you send a request to someone who already requested you, both become buddies automatically.
- Hint text: "Search by full email or name".
- Toast confirmations and translated errors.

**Out of scope:** Invite link (E05-T05).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Searching a full email finds that user; a partial email finds nothing; a name prefix of ≥ 3 letters finds matching users.
- [ ] Each result shows the correct action for the current relation, and it updates right after the action without reload.
- [ ] Sending to someone who already requested you makes you buddies immediately.
- [ ] Empty, loading and no-result states are translated and look calm in both themes.
- [ ] e2e test: A sends, B sees request.

**Depends on:** E05-T01, E02-T04

### E05-T03 · Incoming / outgoing requests — S

**Why:** Users need to act on requests they received and keep track of the ones they sent.

**Scope**
- Buddies page tab **Requests** with two lists:
  - **Incoming:** avatar, name, sent date, **Accept** / **Decline**.
  - **Outgoing:** avatar, name, sent date, **Cancel**.
- Badge on the Buddies nav item with the number of incoming pending requests.
- Optimistic updates with rollback on error.

**Out of scope:** Push/email notifications.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Accepting moves the person to the buddy list immediately and the badge count drops.
- [ ] Declining removes the request from the incoming list; the requester sees it removed from their outgoing list (the reason isn't shown).
- [ ] Cancelling an outgoing request removes it for both users.
- [ ] Badge shows the correct count and is hidden at 0.
- [ ] Empty states for both lists.

**Depends on:** E05-T01

### E05-T04 · Buddy list — S

**Why:** The buddy list is the people you can train with; it should be easy to scan and manage.

**Scope**
- Buddies page tab **Buddies**: avatar, name, "Buddies since {date}", "Last trained together {relative date}" or "Not trained together yet".
- Sorted by last shared session (most recent first), then name.
- Row menu: **Start session with…** (opens E07-T02 with the buddy pre-selected), **View progress together** (E09-T04, when available), **Remove buddy** (confirmation dialog).
- Local filter field when the list has more than 10 buddies.

**Out of scope:** Buddy profile page.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] List shows only accepted buddies in the described order.
- [ ] Removing a buddy requires confirmation and removes them from both users' lists.
- [ ] After removal, past shared sessions and their data stay unchanged for both users.
- [ ] "Start session with…" opens the create form with that buddy already invited.
- [ ] Empty state with an "Add buddy" button.

**Depends on:** E05-T01

### E05-T05 · Invite link — S

**Why:** In the gym it's faster to show a QR code than to type an email.

**Scope**
- Column `profiles.invite_code` (random, URL-safe, unique).
- "Share my invite" in the Add-buddy sheet: shows link `/{locale}/buddies/add/{code}`, a QR code, a copy button and native share (Web Share API).
- Opening the link: if signed out, go through sign-in and come back; then show the inviter's avatar/name and a **Send request** button (or auto-accept if they already requested).
- **Regenerate link** invalidates the old code.

**Out of scope:** Links that expire automatically.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Scanning the QR with a phone opens the link and, after sign-in, shows the inviter with a working "Send request" button.
- [ ] An invalid or regenerated code shows a friendly "Link no longer valid" page.
- [ ] Opening your own link shows "This is your link".
- [ ] Share uses the native share sheet on mobile and copy-to-clipboard on desktop.

**Depends on:** E05-T02

### E05-T06 · In-app notifications for buddy events — S

**Why:** Users should notice new requests and accepted requests without checking the Buddies page.

**Scope**
- Subscribe to `buddy_connections` changes for the current user (Supabase Realtime), plus refetch on window focus.
- Toast when a new request arrives ("Jonas wants to be your gym buddy" with **View**) or when someone accepts yours.
- Updates the nav badge live.

**Out of scope:** Email and push notifications; a notifications inbox.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] When A sends a request, B (with the app open) sees a toast and the badge update within 3 seconds, without reloading.
- [ ] When B accepts, A sees a toast and B appears in A's list.
- [ ] No duplicate toasts for the same event.
- [ ] Works after the phone wakes from sleep (refetch on focus).

**Depends on:** E05-T03

## E06 · Exercise Catalog

**Goal:** A shared catalog of exercises (name, description, machine, tags) that is fast to search and easy to extend from inside a session.  
**Milestone:** M2 · Train together  
**Source:** [epics/E06-exercise-catalog.md](epics/E06-exercise-catalog.md)

### E06-T01 · Catalog schema & seed — M

**Why:** Exercises, machines and tags are the building blocks of every logged set; they need a clean, duplicate-free structure and useful starting content.

**Scope**
- Migrations for `machines`, `exercises`, `tags`, `exercise_tags` plus `exercise_translations` / `machine_translations` (decision Q2) — see [data-model.md](data-model.md).
- `name_normalized` generated columns using `lower(f_unaccent(trim(name)))`.
- Uniqueness: machine `name_normalized`; exercise `(name_normalized, coalesce(machine_id, '00000000-…'))` (same name allowed on different machines, e.g. "Row" on Cable vs Machine).
- Trigram GIN indexes on `name_normalized` for exercises, machines and translation names.
- RLS: all signed-in users can read; insert with `created_by = uid()`; update/delete only own rows; exercises in use (referenced by `session_exercises`) cannot be deleted, only edited.
- Tags are seed-only (users can attach existing tags, not create new ones in MVP) — categories `muscle_group`, `movement`, `equipment`.
- Seed: ~40 tags (EN + LT), ~30 machines/equipment, ~60 common exercises with machine, description and tags, in EN and LT.

**Out of scope:** UI; user-created tags.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `db:reset` creates all tables and seed data; running the seed twice creates no duplicates.
- [ ] Inserting "bench press" when "Bench Press" exists on the same machine fails with a unique violation; on a different machine it succeeds.
- [ ] RLS tests: user B cannot update or delete user A's exercise or machine; anyone signed in can read all.
- [ ] Deleting an exercise that is used in a session fails.
- [ ] Every seeded exercise has at least one tag and both EN and LT names.

**Depends on:** E04-T03

### E06-T02 · Exercise search RPC — S

**Why:** The exercise picker is used in every session; search must be fast, forgiving of typos and accents, and work in both languages.

**Scope**
- `search_exercises(query text, limit int default 20)` SQL function returning `id, name, display_name (for locale), machine_name, tags[], score`.
- Ranking order: exact normalized match → prefix match → trigram similarity (≥ 0.3) → description contains query. Ties: exercises the caller used most recently, then alphabetically.
- Searches original names and translations; accent- and case-insensitive.
- `recent_exercises(limit int default 8)`: the caller's most recently logged exercises.
- Query length < 2 returns an empty result (UI shows recents instead).

**Out of scope:** Full-text search on long descriptions.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] "spaud" finds "Spaudimas gulint"; "bench" finds "Bench press"; "benhc" (typo) still finds "Bench press".
- [ ] An exact match is always ranked first.
- [ ] Results include machine name and tags, so no extra request is needed per result.
- [ ] p95 under 100 ms with 10 000 exercises (seeded load test with `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` in the PR).
- [ ] `recent_exercises` returns only the caller's exercises, newest first, without duplicates.

**Depends on:** E06-T01

### E06-T03 · Exercise picker (autocomplete) — M

**Why:** This is the main way users add exercises to a session: a searchable dropdown with suggestions and a button to create a new exercise when nothing is found.

**Scope**
- `ExercisePicker` built on the Combobox (E02-T04), backed by `search_exercises` and `recent_exercises`.
- Before typing: section "Recently used" (up to 8). While typing: ranked results.
- Each result: exercise name (bold match), machine name (muted), up to 3 tag chips.
- When there's no exact normalized match: footer button **"+ Create '{query}'"**, which opens the create form (E06-T04) with the name pre-filled.
- Props: `onSelect(exercise)`, `excludeIds` (already in the session; shown as "Already added" and selectable to jump to it).

**Out of scope:** The create form itself (E06-T04).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Opening the picker without typing shows the user's recent exercises (or popular seeded ones for new users).
- [ ] Typing shows ranked results within 300 ms of the last keystroke on a normal connection.
- [ ] "Create '{query}'" appears only when no exact normalized match exists, and opens the form with the name pre-filled.
- [ ] Exercises already in the session are marked "Already added".
- [ ] Fully usable by keyboard and on a 360 px phone screen.

**Depends on:** E06-T02, E02-T04

### E06-T04 · Create / edit exercise form — M

**Why:** When an exercise isn't in the catalog, users must be able to add it in a few seconds without leaving the session.

**Scope**
- Form in a sheet (mobile) / dialog (desktop) with fields:
  - **Name** (required, 2–80 chars)
  - **Description** (optional, ≤ 500 chars)
  - **Machine** (optional; Combobox with create-new, E06-T06)
  - **Tags** (optional; multi-select Combobox of existing tags). Auto-suggested tags (E06-T05) are pre-selected and marked "suggested"; they update as name/machine change until the user edits tags manually.
- Zod schema shared between client and Server Action.
- Duplicate check before submit (debounced) and on save: "This exercise already exists" with **Use existing**.
- After creating from the picker, the new exercise is selected and the user returns to the session.
- Edit mode for exercises the user created (same form). Non-owners see read-only details.

**Out of scope:** Images/videos; deleting exercises (only unused own exercises can be deleted, from the library page).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Creating an exercise from the picker takes the user back to the session with the new exercise added.
- [ ] An empty or 1-character name shows a translated validation error and nothing is saved.
- [ ] Entering an existing name (any case or accents) on the same machine shows the duplicate message with a working **Use existing**.
- [ ] Suggested tags appear for names like "Bench press" and can be removed before saving.
- [ ] Only the creator sees the Edit action; others can view but not edit.
- [ ] Saved data shows correctly in the picker and library right away.

**Depends on:** E06-T03, E06-T05

### E06-T05 · Rule-based auto-tagging — S

**Why:** Tags make search and dashboards (per muscle group) useful, but users rarely add them by hand; auto-suggestions fill the gap.

**Scope**
- `lib/tags/autoTag(name: string, machineName?: string): TagSlug[]` — pure function.
- Rule dictionary (`lib/tags/rules.ts`) of keyword stems in EN and LT → tag slugs, e.g.:
  - `bench|chest|fly|krūtin|spaudimas gulint` → `chest`, `push`
  - `squat|leg press|pritūp|kojų` → `legs`, `quads`
  - `row|pull|lat|trauk` → `back`, `pull`
  - `curl|bicep|bicepsas` → `biceps`; `tricep|dip|pushdown` → `triceps`
  - Machine-based: `dumbbell|hantel` → `dumbbell`; `barbell|štang` → `barbell`; `cable|lyn` → `cable`
- Accent-insensitive, word-boundary-aware matching; returns unique slugs, max 5.
- Saved with `source = 'auto'`; tags the user adds are `source = 'manual'`.
- Tags the user removed are remembered on the form so they aren't re-added during the same edit.

**Out of scope:** AI tagging (post-MVP, Q10).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Fixture test: at least 90% of seeded exercises get at least one correct tag, and none get a clearly wrong muscle group.
- [ ] "Spaudimas gulint" and "Bench press" both produce `chest` and `push`.
- [ ] "Squash" does not produce `legs` (word boundaries respected).
- [ ] Function runs on both client (live suggestions) and server, with no network calls.
- [ ] Adding a keyword rule requires only editing `rules.ts` (documented in the file).

**Depends on:** E06-T01

### E06-T06 · Machine management — S

**Why:** Many exercises depend on the machine (e.g. "Chest press" on two different machines); users need to pick or add machines easily.

**Scope**
- `MachinePicker` (Combobox) backed by a `search_machines(query)` RPC (same ranking idea as exercises).
- "+ Create '{query}'" creates a machine with just a name (2–60 chars) in one tap, with a duplicate check by normalized name.
- Machines created by the user can be renamed by them (from the library page).

**Out of scope:** Machine photos, gym location of machines.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Typing "smith" suggests "Smith machine"; "hantel" suggests "Hanteliai / Dumbbells".
- [ ] Creating a new machine selects it in the exercise form immediately.
- [ ] Creating "smith machine" when "Smith Machine" exists selects the existing one instead of creating a duplicate.
- [ ] RLS: only the creator can rename a machine.

**Depends on:** E06-T01, E02-T04

### E06-T07 · Exercise library page — S

**Why:** Outside sessions, users want to browse exercises, check details and jump to their progress for one exercise.

**Scope**
- Page `/[locale]/exercises` (linked from Progress and the avatar menu): search field, filters by tag (multi, AND) and machine, toggle "Only exercises I've done".
- Infinite scroll / pagination (30 per page).
- Exercise detail page: name, machine, description, tags, created by (name or "Gym Tracker" for seeded), "My last attempt" summary, link **View my progress** (E09-T03), Edit/Delete for owners (delete only if unused).

**Out of scope:** Favorites.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Filtering by "legs" + "barbell" shows only exercises with both tags.
- [ ] Search and filters are kept in the URL (back button restores them).
- [ ] Scrolling 300+ exercises stays smooth on a mid-range phone.
- [ ] Detail page shows the user's last attempt if one exists.
- [ ] Owner can delete an unused exercise; a used exercise shows "Can't delete: used in sessions".

**Depends on:** E06-T02

---

## E07 · Gym Sessions

**Goal:** Users create gym sessions, invite gym buddies, and move sessions through planned → active → completed.  
**Milestone:** M2 · Train together  
**Source:** [epics/E07-gym-sessions.md](epics/E07-gym-sessions.md)

### E07-T01 · Session schema, RLS & lifecycle — M

**Why:** Sessions define who can see and log which data, so the rules for membership, invites and status must be enforced in the database.

**Scope**
- Migrations for `gym_sessions` and `session_participants` (see [data-model.md](data-model.md#gym_sessions)); `invite_status` adds `removed` and `left` (Q4).
- Trigger: on session insert, add the owner as participant with role `owner`, `invite_status = accepted`.
- `is_session_member(session, user)` — accepted participant (`security definer`, `stable`).
- Status transitions enforced by a trigger: `planned → active | cancelled`, `active → completed | cancelled`, `completed → active` (reopen, only within the edit window). `started_at`/`completed_at` set automatically.
- RLS:
  - Sessions: SELECT for members and invited users; INSERT with `owner_id = uid()`; UPDATE of details by owner; status change by any member.
  - Participants: SELECT for members/invitees of that session; INSERT (invite) only by owner, only for buddies (`are_buddies`); invitee updates own `invite_status` (`invited → accepted | declined`, `accepted → left`); owner can set `removed`.
- Extend `profiles` SELECT policy to co-participants.

**Out of scope:** UI; edit lock (E07-T06).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Creating a session adds the owner as an accepted participant automatically.
- [ ] Inviting a user who is not the owner's buddy fails (RLS test).
- [ ] A non-member cannot see the session or its participant list.
- [ ] Invalid transitions (e.g. `completed → planned`, `cancelled → active`) are rejected with a clear error.
- [ ] Only the invitee can accept/decline their invitation; only the owner can remove a participant.
- [ ] `started_at` and `completed_at` are filled in when status changes.

**Depends on:** E05-T01

### E07-T02 · Create session — M

**Why:** Starting a workout should take seconds, whether planning ahead or starting right now with friends.

**Scope**
- "New session" from Home and Sessions page (and "Start session with…" on a buddy).
- Form: **When** (date/time, default now), **Title** (optional; placeholder shows the generated default), **Location** (optional, free text with last used locations as suggestions), **Invite buddies** (multi-select Combobox of buddies).
- Two submit buttons: **Start now** (status `active`) and **Plan** (status `planned`, enabled when time is in the future).
- Default title by locale and weekday: "Antradienio treniruotė" / "Tuesday session".
- Warn (not block) if the user already has an active session: "You have an active session. Continue it instead?"

**Out of scope:** Recurring sessions, templates.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A solo session can be started with one tap after opening the form (all defaults).
- [ ] Invited buddies see the invitation in their Invitations tab.
- [ ] Only buddies appear in the invite picker.
- [ ] **Plan** with a past time shows a validation error; **Start now** always works.
- [ ] After saving, the user lands on the session page.
- [ ] The default title is in the active language and matches the weekday.

**Depends on:** E07-T01, E02-T04

### E07-T03 · Sessions list — S

**Why:** Users need a quick overview of the current session, what's coming and what they've done.

**Scope**
- Sessions page with tabs:
  - **Upcoming:** active session pinned on top with **Continue**, then planned sessions ascending by time.
  - **Invitations:** pending invites with **Accept** / **Decline** (E07-T04).
  - **History:** completed sessions, newest first, paginated (20 per page); cancelled sessions shown muted with a "Cancelled" label.
- Session card: date/time, title, location, participant AvatarStack, status chip, number of exercises (history).
- Badge on the Sessions nav item for pending invitations.

**Out of scope:** Calendar view (part of E09-T05).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] An active session always appears first in Upcoming with a working **Continue** button.
- [ ] Each tab has a translated empty state with a relevant action.
- [ ] History loads more items on scroll without duplicates.
- [ ] Invitation badge count matches the Invitations tab.

**Depends on:** E07-T01

### E07-T04 · Respond to invitations — S

**Why:** Invited buddies decide whether to join; once they join they can log in the session.

**Scope**
- Accept / Decline on the Invitations tab and on the session page (an invited user sees a read-only preview with a banner: "Jonas invited you. Join?").
- **Leave session** for accepted participants (not the owner), with confirmation.
- The owner sees each participant's status (invited / accepted / declined / left).

**Out of scope:** Notifications outside the app.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] After accepting, the session appears in the user's Upcoming tab and they can log sets in it.
- [ ] After declining, the invitation disappears for the invitee and the owner sees "Declined".
- [ ] A participant who leaves can no longer see the session; their already logged sets stay in their own history.
- [ ] The owner cannot leave their own session (can cancel it instead).

**Depends on:** E07-T01

### E07-T05 · Session detail & management — M

**Why:** The session page is the hub of a workout: who's there, its state, and the actions to start, finish or change it.

**Scope**
- Session page header: title, date/time, location, status chip, participants (avatars with status), menu with actions.
- Owner actions: edit details, invite more buddies, remove a participant, cancel session.
- Any participant: **Start** (planned → active), **Complete** (active → completed, with confirmation and short summary "5 exercises · 42 sets"), **Reopen** (within edit window).
- Below the header: the exercise list / logging area (E08).
- After **Complete**, navigate to the session summary (E09-T02).
- Cancelled sessions are read-only with a banner.

**Out of scope:** Logging UI (E08).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Only the owner sees edit, invite, remove and cancel actions.
- [ ] Removing a participant revokes their access; their already logged sets are kept and still count in their own history (see [open-questions.md](open-questions.md) Q4).
- [ ] Completing shows a confirmation and then the session summary.
- [ ] Cancelled sessions show a banner and no edit controls.
- [ ] Participants see status changes from others after a refresh (live updates come in E08-T07).

**Depends on:** E07-T01

### E07-T06 · Edit lock after completion — S

**Why:** Training history should be trustworthy; users can fix typos for a while, but old sessions shouldn't change (decision D7).

**Scope**
- SQL function `is_session_editable(session)`: status not `cancelled`, and if `completed`, `completed_at > now() - interval '7 days'`.
- Used in RLS write policies for `session_exercises`, `session_sets`, `session_exercise_notes` and for session reopen.
- Server Actions return `LOCKED` error code → translated "This session is locked for editing".
- UI hides edit controls and shows "Locked · completed {date}" on locked sessions.

**Out of scope:** Admin override.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Sets can be added/edited 6 days after completion and are rejected 8 days after (DB test with mocked time).
- [ ] A locked session shows no edit controls in the UI.
- [ ] Trying to write through the API returns the `LOCKED` error and the translated message.
- [ ] Reopen is not offered for locked sessions.

**Depends on:** E07-T01

### E07-T07 · Home screen — S

**Why:** Home should get users into their workout in one tap and show what needs attention.

**Scope**
- Home sections (only shown if relevant):
  1. **Active session** card with **Continue**.
  2. **Next planned session** with time and participants.
  3. **Invitations** count with link (sessions + buddy requests).
  4. **Recent sessions** (last 3 completed) with link to their summaries.
  5. Primary button **Start session**.
- New-user empty state: 3 steps — "Add a gym buddy", "Start your first session", "Log your first set".

**Out of scope:** Progress tiles (E09-T05).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] With an active session, Continue is the most visible element and opens the session page.
- [ ] A brand-new user sees the onboarding steps, and each opens the right screen.
- [ ] Home loads in under 1 second on 4G (server-rendered, one query per section or fewer).
- [ ] All counts match the corresponding pages.

**Depends on:** E07-T03

## E08 · Session Logging

**Goal:** Inside a session, participants add exercises and log weight, reps and notes for every person, with each person's last attempt loaded automatically.  
**Milestone:** M2 · Train together  
**Source:** [epics/E08-session-logging.md](epics/E08-session-logging.md)

### E08-T01 · Logging schema & RLS — M

**Why:** Sets and notes are the core data of the app; they must be correct, private to session members, and record who entered them.

**Scope**
- Migrations for `session_exercises`, `session_sets`, `session_exercise_notes` (see [data-model.md](data-model.md)).
- `session_sets.session_id` and `session_exercise_notes.session_id` filled by trigger from `session_exercise_id` (used by RLS and realtime filters).
- `set_number` assigned automatically per `(session_exercise_id, user_id)`; renumbered when a set is deleted.
- `recorded_by` / `updated_by` always set from `uid()` by trigger (client values ignored).
- Unique `(session_id, exercise_id)` in `session_exercises`.
- RLS: read for session members; write for session members when `is_session_editable(session)`; `user_id` of a set/note must be an accepted participant of that session.
- Indexes for last-attempt and progress queries: `session_sets (user_id, session_exercise_id)`, `session_exercises (exercise_id, session_id)`.

**Out of scope:** UI.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] RLS tests: non-members cannot read or write; members can write for any accepted participant (D2).
- [ ] Logging a set for someone who isn't an accepted participant fails.
- [ ] A client sending `recorded_by = someone else` still gets `recorded_by = uid()`.
- [ ] Deleting set 2 of 3 renumbers the remaining sets to 1 and 2.
- [ ] Writes to cancelled or locked sessions fail.
- [ ] Weight < 0, reps < 1 or reps > 999 are rejected by check constraints.

**Depends on:** E07-T01, E06-T01

### E08-T02 · Add exercise to session — S

**Why:** A session is a list of exercises; adding one must be quick and lead straight into logging.

**Scope**
- **Add exercise** button (sticky at the bottom of the session page) opens the ExercisePicker (E06-T03) including "Create new".
- The selected exercise becomes a new card at the end, opened for logging; the page scrolls to it.
- Card menu: **Move up/down** (mobile), drag handle (desktop), **Remove** (confirmation if any sets exist; deletes its sets and notes).
- Choosing an exercise that is already in the session scrolls to and opens the existing card.

**Out of scope:** Supersets / grouping.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Adding an exercise takes at most 3 taps when it's in "Recently used".
- [ ] The same exercise can't appear twice in a session; choosing it again opens the existing card.
- [ ] Reordering persists after reload for all participants.
- [ ] Removing a card with sets asks for confirmation and removes the sets for everyone.
- [ ] Not available on locked/cancelled sessions.

**Depends on:** E08-T01, E06-T03

### E08-T03 · Last attempt RPC — S

**Why:** Seeing what you lifted last time is the main reason people track workouts; the query must be fast and follow decision D6.

**Scope**
- `last_attempt(exercise uuid, users text[], exclude_session uuid)` returning, per user: `session_id`, `session_date`, list of sets (`set_number`, `weight_kg`, `reps`), and `note`.
- "Last" = most recent session (by `started_at`, fallback `scheduled_at`) other than `exclude_session` in which that user has at least one set for the exercise. Cancelled sessions are ignored.
- One call returns data for all participants (avoids N requests).
- Only returns data for users the caller can see (session co-participants), via security-definer checks.

**Out of scope:** "Best ever" attempt (E09).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Returns an empty entry for a user who has never done the exercise.
- [ ] Ignores the current session, cancelled sessions, and sessions where the user has no sets for the exercise.
- [ ] Returns data for all requested participants in one call.
- [ ] A caller cannot get last attempts of users who aren't in the session with them.
- [ ] Responds in under 50 ms for a user with 2 years of data (index check in PR).

**Depends on:** E08-T01

### E08-T04 · Exercise card with per-participant logging — M

**Why:** This is where users spend most of their time in the gym; logging sets for each person must be fast, clear and one-handed.

**Scope**
- Exercise card (expanded): name, machine, tags; **participant switcher** (avatars as a SegmentedControl; defaults to the current user).
- For the selected participant:
  - Set list: `#`, weight, reps; tap a set to edit inline; swipe or menu to delete.
  - **Add set** row: weight and reps NumberSteppers + **✓ Add** button.
- Collapsed card: one summary line per participant, e.g. "Jonas · 3 × 8 @ 60 kg", "Ona · 4 × 10 @ 25 kg".
- Only one card expanded at a time; expanding scrolls it into view.
- Optimistic updates (TanStack Query) with rollback and a toast on error.
- Haptic feedback on add (where supported).

**Out of scope:** Last-attempt pre-fill (E08-T05), notes (E08-T06), realtime (E08-T07).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Logging a set when values are pre-filled takes 1 tap (**Add**); changing weight and adding takes ≤ 3 taps.
- [ ] Switching participant shows that person's sets and inputs without reloading.
- [ ] Editing and deleting a set work and are kept after reload.
- [ ] A failed save shows the set as failed with **Retry**, and nothing is lost.
- [ ] Usable one-handed on a 360 px phone: Add button and steppers in the lower half of the screen.
- [ ] Collapsed summaries are correct for every participant (unit test of summary formatter, both locales).

**Depends on:** E08-T02, E02-T05

### E08-T05 · Auto-load last attempt — M

**Why:** Pre-filling last time's numbers saves typing and shows the target to beat — a key requirement.

**Scope**
- When an exercise card is opened, fetch `last_attempt` for all accepted participants in one request (prefetched when the card is added or the session loads).
- Show a muted reference block per participant: "Last time · 12 Nov: 60×8, 60×8, 57,5×7".
- Pre-fill the **Add set** inputs:
  - Set N → last attempt's set N.
  - After last attempt's set count, or if no last attempt: repeat the participant's previous set in this session.
  - No history at all: weight empty, reps 10 (placeholder).
- **Copy all** button: logs all last-attempt sets at once as new sets (editable afterwards).
- Clear visual difference between reference values (muted, italic label "Last time") and logged values.
- Link on the reference block to that previous session's summary.

**Out of scope:** Progression suggestions (e.g. "+2.5 kg").

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Opening an exercise shows each participant's last attempt and the inputs pre-filled within 300 ms (data prefetched).
- [ ] For set 2, inputs show last time's set 2; for set 4 when last time had 3 sets, inputs repeat this session's set 3.
- [ ] A participant who never did the exercise sees "First time" and empty weight.
- [ ] **Copy all** creates the same number of sets with the same values, and they can be edited.
- [ ] Reference values can never be mistaken for logged sets (design review in both themes).

**Depends on:** E08-T03, E08-T04

### E08-T06 · Notes per participant per exercise — S

**Why:** Lifters note things like seat height, grip or pain; notes per person per exercise help next time.

**Scope**
- Notes field (Textarea, collapsible "Add note") in each participant's section of the card.
- Autosave 800 ms after typing stops, plus on blur; status "Saving…" / "Saved".
- Max 1000 characters with counter after 800.
- Last attempt's note shown in the reference block ("Last note: seat 4").
- Anyone in the session can edit any participant's note (D2); `updated_by` shown as a small avatar if not the participant.

**Out of scope:** Session-level notes; rich text.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Typing a note and leaving the page without clicking anything still saves it.
- [ ] The 1001st character is not accepted and the counter warns from 800.
- [ ] Last time's note is visible when logging the same exercise in the next session.
- [ ] Concurrent edits: the last save wins and the other user sees the update (after E08-T07).

**Depends on:** E08-T01, E08-T04

### E08-T07 · Realtime sync between participants — M

**Why:** Buddies often log on their own phones; everyone should see the same session without refreshing.

**Scope**
- Supabase Realtime channel per session (`session:{id}`) listening to inserts/updates/deletes on `session_exercises`, `session_sets`, `session_exercise_notes`, `session_participants` and the session row, filtered by `session_id`.
- Merge events into the TanStack Query cache; ignore echoes of the user's own optimistic changes (match by client-generated id).
- Show a small avatar on sets recorded by someone else.
- Presence: avatars of participants currently viewing the session.
- Reconnect handling: on reconnect or tab focus, refetch the session.
- Connection indicator only when offline ("Offline – changes will sync").

**Out of scope:** Full offline mode with a queue (post-MVP).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] A set logged on phone A appears on phone B within 2 seconds.
- [ ] No duplicate sets appear on the phone that logged them.
- [ ] Exercise reorders, new exercises and status changes (e.g. completed) also sync.
- [ ] After turning flight mode on and off, the session refreshes and shows all changes.
- [ ] Users who aren't members receive no events (RLS on realtime verified).
- [ ] e2e test with two browser contexts.

**Depends on:** E08-T04

### E08-T08 · Personal record highlight — S

**Why:** A small celebration of a new best motivates users, without making the UI loud.

**Scope**
- When a set is logged, compare it to the participant's previous best for that exercise (from sessions before this one): **weight PR** (heaviest weight at ≥ 1 rep) and **e1RM PR** (Epley).
- Show a small muted-ochre "PR" chip on the set and a short toast "New personal record: 62,5 kg".
- Uses the shared metrics library (E09-T01); previous bests prefetched with the last attempt.
- First-ever attempt is not a PR.

**Out of scope:** PR history page (part of E09-T03).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Logging a heavier weight than ever before shows the PR chip and toast once.
- [ ] Editing the set down below the record removes the chip.
- [ ] Bodyweight (0 kg) exercises use reps PR instead of weight.
- [ ] Results match E09 dashboards for the same data (shared tests).
- [ ] No bright colors or large animations (design review).

**Depends on:** E08-T04, E09-T01

---

## E09 · Progress Dashboards

**Goal:** Overview pages with multiple slices — user per session and user per exercise — so progress over time is easy to see.  
**Milestone:** M3 · See progress  
**Source:** [epics/E09-progress-dashboards.md](epics/E09-progress-dashboards.md)

### E09-T01 · Metrics library & RPCs — M

**Why:** Every dashboard, PR badge and comparison must calculate numbers the same way; one definition avoids confusing differences.

**Scope**
- Metric definitions (TS in `lib/metrics`, mirrored in SQL):
  - **Top set**: heaviest weight in a session (tie → more reps).
  - **Estimated 1RM** (Epley): `w × (1 + reps / 30)`, only for reps ≤ 12; `w` when reps = 1.
  - **Volume**: Σ weight × reps.
  - **Total reps**, **set count**.
  - **Bodyweight exercises** (all weights 0): use total reps and max reps instead.
  - **PR**: a session's metric higher than all earlier sessions.
- RPCs:
  - `exercise_progress(exercise, user, from, to)` → one row per session: date, session_id, top set, best e1RM, volume, total reps, sets, is_pr flags.
  - `session_summary(session, user)` → per exercise: sets, volume, top set, delta vs last attempt, PR flags; plus totals and duration.
- Access: own data, or a co-participant's data only for shared sessions (D8).
- Fixture dataset (seed script `db:seed:demo`) with ~6 months of realistic data for 3 users.

**Out of scope:** Charts.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] TS and SQL produce identical results on the fixture dataset (shared test).
- [ ] e1RM for 100 kg × 5 = 116,7 kg; for reps > 12 e1RM is not calculated.
- [ ] Bodyweight exercises return reps-based metrics and no weight PRs.
- [ ] A user cannot get progress for someone else's non-shared sessions (RLS test).
- [ ] `exercise_progress` for 1 year of data responds in under 150 ms.

**Depends on:** E08-T01

### E09-T02 · Dashboard: user per session — M

**Why:** Right after a workout and later in history, users want a clear summary of what they did and whether they improved.

**Scope**
- Page `/[locale]/progress/session/[sessionId]`.
- Participant switcher (defaults to the current user; other participants of the session can be selected).
- Totals: duration, exercises, sets, total volume, number of PRs.
- Per exercise: sets list, top set, volume, delta vs last attempt (↑ / ↓ / = with value, muted colors), PR chips, note.
- Link from each exercise to its progress page (E09-T03).
- Shown after **Complete session** and reachable from History and Home.

**Out of scope:** Sharing the summary outside the app.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Totals and per-exercise numbers match the logged sets (fixture test).
- [ ] Delta arrows compare to the participant's last attempt (D6); "First time" when there's none.
- [ ] Switching participant shows that person's summary for the same session.
- [ ] Non-participants get a 404.
- [ ] Readable on a 360 px phone in both themes and languages.

**Depends on:** E09-T01, E07-T05

### E09-T03 · Dashboard: user per exercise — M

**Why:** The main progress view: how one exercise developed over time.

**Scope**
- Page `/[locale]/progress/exercise/[exerciseId]`.
- Exercise selector (Combobox limited to exercises the user has logged) at the top.
- Metric selector: **Top weight**, **Est. 1RM**, **Volume**, **Total reps** (bodyweight: reps metrics only).
- Range selector: 1M / 3M / 6M / 1Y / All (default 3M).
- Line chart (Recharts, chart tokens) with PR points marked; tooltip with date, value and sets.
- Stat tiles: current best, change over the selected range (absolute and %), number of sessions.
- History table: date, sets (e.g. "60×8, 60×8, 57,5×7"), top set, volume, note; newest first; paginated.
- Selected metric and range stored in URL params.

**Out of scope:** Buddy comparison (E09-T04).

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Chart, tiles and table show the same data for the selected range and metric.
- [ ] Tapping a chart point or table row opens that session's summary.
- [ ] With fewer than 2 sessions, a friendly empty state replaces the chart ("Log this exercise again to see progress").
- [ ] Chart is readable in both themes, at 360 px, and has an accessible text alternative (table).
- [ ] Changing metric/range doesn't reload the page and can be shared via URL.

**Depends on:** E09-T01

### E09-T04 · Compare with buddy — S

**Why:** Training together is motivating; comparing progress with a buddy on the same exercise adds to that, within privacy limits.

**Scope**
- "Compare with" selector on the exercise progress page listing buddies who have logged this exercise in sessions shared with the user.
- Overlays the buddy's series (different chart token, legend with names/avatars); tiles show both users side by side.
- Only data from shared sessions is used for the buddy (D8).
- Option to show values as % change from the start of the range (fairer comparison between different strength levels).

**Out of scope:** Leaderboards; comparing more than one buddy.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Only buddies with shared sessions for this exercise can be selected.
- [ ] The buddy's series contains only shared-session data (RLS + fixture test).
- [ ] The two series use clearly different, calm colors, with a legend, in both themes.
- [ ] "% change" mode starts both lines at 0%.

**Depends on:** E09-T03

### E09-T05 · Progress overview page — M

**Why:** Users need an entry point to see all their progress at a glance and drill into slices.

**Scope**
- Page `/[locale]/progress` with summary tiles: sessions this month (vs last month), total volume this month, weekly streak (weeks in a row with ≥ 1 session), PRs this month.
- Slice tabs:
  - **By exercise:** list of logged exercises with sparkline (last 8 sessions, top weight or e1RM), latest top set, trend arrow, last date; sortable by last done / most improved / name.
  - **By session:** activity heatmap/calendar (last 12 months, earth-tone scale) + list of sessions linking to summaries.
- Each item links to the matching detail dashboard (E09-T02 / E09-T03).
- One RPC per tab (`progress_overview_exercises`, `progress_overview_sessions`) to keep it fast.

**Out of scope:** Body weight / body measurements tracking.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Tiles, sparklines and calendar match the underlying data (fixture test).
- [ ] Page loads in under 1 second for a user with 300 sessions.
- [ ] Every list item and calendar day with a session navigates to the correct detail view.
- [ ] Empty state for new users with a link to start a session.
- [ ] Calendar colors pass contrast against the background in both themes.

**Depends on:** E09-T02, E09-T03

### E09-T06 · Filters by tag / muscle group — S

**Why:** Users want to see progress for a muscle group (e.g. legs), not only one exercise at a time.

**Scope**
- Tag filter (multi-select chips, muscle-group tags first) on the overview page.
- Filters the **By exercise** list, the volume tile and the calendar intensity (volume of matching exercises only).
- Filter kept in the URL (`?tags=legs,back`).

**Out of scope:** Custom saved views.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Selecting "legs" shows only exercises tagged legs and recalculates volume for them only.
- [ ] Multiple tags combine as OR (any matching tag), clearly labeled in the UI.
- [ ] Reloading or sharing the URL keeps the filter.
- [ ] Clearing filters restores the full overview.

**Depends on:** E09-T05

---

## E10 · Quality, Privacy & Launch

**Goal:** The MVP is accessible, fast, private and observable before public launch.  
**Milestone:** M4 · Launch  
**Source:** [epics/E10-quality-launch.md](epics/E10-quality-launch.md)

### E10-T01 · End-to-end happy path suite — M

**Why:** The full shared-workout flow touches every epic; one automated run proves it all works together before each release.

**Scope**
- Playwright scenarios with two test users (A and B) in separate browser contexts:
  1. A and B sign in (testing tokens).
  2. A finds B and sends a buddy request; B accepts.
  3. A creates a session and invites B; B accepts.
  4. A adds an existing exercise; B creates a new exercise from the picker.
  5. A logs sets for A and B; B logs a set and a note on their own phone; both see each other's changes.
  6. A completes the session; both view the session summary.
  7. Second session: last attempt is pre-filled; A logs a heavier set → PR chip.
  8. A opens the exercise progress dashboard and sees two data points.
- Smoke run of key pages in `lt` + dark and `en` + light.
- Mobile viewport (iPhone) and desktop.

**Out of scope:** Load testing.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] All scenarios pass in CI on every PR to `main`.
- [ ] 20 consecutive CI runs pass without retries (no flaky tests).
- [ ] Failure output includes screenshot, trace and the step that failed.
- [ ] Suite runs in under 6 minutes.

**Depends on:** E09-T03

### E10-T02 · Accessibility audit — S

**Why:** The app must be usable by everyone, including keyboard and screen-reader users, in both themes.

**Scope**
- `@axe-core/playwright` checks on: landing, Home, Buddies, Sessions, session logging, exercise form, all dashboards — in both themes.
- Manual checks: VoiceOver on iOS (log a set end-to-end), keyboard-only on desktop, 200% zoom, `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Contrast re-check of final colors, including charts and calendar.
- Fix issues or create follow-up tasks with severity.

**Out of scope:** Formal certification.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Zero critical or serious axe violations on the listed pages in both themes.
- [ ] A set can be logged end-to-end with VoiceOver and with keyboard only.
- [ ] Layout works at 200% zoom without lost content.
- [ ] All findings fixed or ticketed with an owner.

**Depends on:** E10-T01

### E10-T03 · Performance pass — S

**Why:** The app is used on phones in gyms with weak signal; it must feel instant.

**Scope**
- Lighthouse (mobile, throttled 4G) for landing, Home, session logging and Progress overview.
- Bundle analysis (`@next/bundle-analyzer`); lazy-load charts and heavy pickers.
- `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` for all RPCs on the demo dataset scaled ×10; add missing indexes.
- Measure set-logging round-trip time (p95) on preview.

**Out of scope:** CDN or infrastructure changes beyond Vercel/Supabase defaults.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] LCP < 2.5 s and Lighthouse performance ≥ 90 on the four pages.
- [ ] Set logging round-trip p95 < 300 ms.
- [ ] No RPC over 150 ms on the scaled dataset.
- [ ] First-load JS for the session page under 200 kB (gzipped).

**Depends on:** E10-T01

### E10-T04 · Security review — S

**Why:** The app stores personal training data and shares it between users; a final review confirms the protections hold.

**Scope**
- Checklist review of RLS for every table and operation (select/insert/update/delete) against the data-model doc; fill any test gaps.
- Confirm the service-role key is only used in the webhook/admin module.
- Webhook signature verification and replay handling.
- Rate limits on `search_users`, exercise/machine creation and buddy requests (e.g. Upstash or Postgres-based counter).
- Security headers (CSP, HSTS, frame-ancestors), dependency audit (`npm audit`, Dependabot).
- Check that no private data (emails, notes) appears in logs or error tracking.

**Out of scope:** External penetration test.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Every table has RLS tests for all four operations.
- [ ] Rate limits return a translated "Too many requests" after the threshold.
- [ ] Security headers score A on securityheaders.com (or equivalent check).
- [ ] No high or critical dependency vulnerabilities open.
- [ ] Review notes stored in `docs/security-review.md`.

**Depends on:** E10-T01

### E10-T05 · Privacy & account deletion — M

**Why:** EU users (GDPR) have the right to see and delete their data; it's also simply expected.

**Scope**
- Privacy policy page (EN/LT): what is stored, who can see it (buddies, session co-participants), retention, contact.
- **Export my data** (Settings): JSON download of profile, buddies (names only), sessions, exercises created, sets and notes.
- **Delete account** (Settings): confirmation by typing a word; deletes the Clerk user, which triggers `user.deleted`:
  - Delete profile, buddy connections, participations, own sets and notes.
  - Sessions owned by the user: ownership moves to another accepted participant, or the session is deleted if none.
  - Exercises/machines created by the user are kept with `created_by = null`.
- Data retention note in docs.

**Out of scope:** Data import.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Export contains all of the user's sessions, sets and notes, and opens as valid JSON.
- [ ] After deletion, no row in any table references the user id (automated test).
- [ ] Buddies still see their own sets in shared sessions; the deleted user appears as "Deleted user".
- [ ] Deletion completes within 1 minute.
- [ ] Privacy policy is linked from the landing page and Settings in both languages.

**Depends on:** E04-T03, E08-T01

### E10-T06 · Installable PWA shell — S

**Why:** Opening the app from the home screen like a native app makes it faster to use in the gym.

**Scope**
- Web app manifest (name, short name, icons in earth tones, `display: standalone`, start URL `/`).
- Apple touch icons and splash screens; `theme-color` per mode.
- Minimal service worker caching static assets (no offline data sync).
- Gentle "Add to Home Screen" hint after the second completed session (dismissible, not shown again).

**Out of scope:** Offline logging, push notifications.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Installable on Android Chrome (install prompt) and iOS Safari (Add to Home Screen).
- [ ] Opens full-screen with the correct icon and theme color.
- [ ] Lighthouse PWA "installable" check passes.
- [ ] The hint appears at most once and can be dismissed.

**Depends on:** E02-T06

### E10-T07 · Launch checklist — S

**Why:** A short, explicit checklist prevents forgotten production settings on launch day.

**Scope**
- Production Clerk instance with verified Google OAuth consent screen (app name, logo, privacy policy URL).
- Custom domain + HTTPS; Clerk and Supabase configured for it.
- Supabase production: point-in-time recovery/backups enabled, seed data loaded, connection limits checked.
- Error tracking alerts (new error types, error spikes) to the team channel; uptime check.
- Analytics (privacy-friendly) for the success metrics in the vision doc.
- Smoke test on production with a real Google account.

**Out of scope:** Marketing activities.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Every checklist item is checked off with a link or screenshot as evidence.
- [ ] A real Google account can sign in on production and complete the happy path.
- [ ] A restore from backup has been tested once on staging.
- [ ] The product owner signs off the launch.

**Depends on:** E10-T02, E10-T03, E10-T04, E10-T05
